messages.subject: Random Effects in Prediction
parts:
Hello,

I have a glmm gamma hurdle model with fixed effects and 3 random factor effects. I am making predictions using a prediction stack and do not want to include the random effects, do I need to include the random effect covariates in the stack and formula but set all of the values to NA? i.e do the estimation and prediction stacks need to have the same covariates?

Cheers,
Sylvan

messages.author: 5063972801d34964
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random Effects in Prediction
parts:
The easiest way is to create a new random effect level in each group for every row of your prediction set (e.g., 0 or some other unused value) and then the new level is automatically set to the mean value of 0 and you get your population level estimates. 

Jonathan
